children: , Google's search, advertising and cloud-computing powerhouse, rose roughly 0.7% to $334.14 Wednesday despite scoring a major courtroom win. A federal judge rejected the Justice Department's demand to break off Google's AdX advertising exchange, where publishers pay a 20% fee on completed transactions.

This was not a clean regulatory escape. The earlier ruling that Google maintained illegal advertising-technology monopolies still stands, and Judge Leonie Brinkema accepted most of the government's proposed operating restrictions. The financial machine remains formidable: Alphabet's second-quarter filing showed revenue jumping 24% to $119.8 billion, powered by $94.5 billion from Google Services.

Google Services generated nearly 79% of total quarterly revenue, making control of the advertising pipeline critical to Alphabet's profit engine. Investors are already paying up for that dominance: the $334.14 share price stands 32.68% above the $251.83 GF Value estimate. The breakup threat just took another serious hitbut regulatory restrictions, appeals and a stretched valuation keep the pressure firmly on.

title: Alphabet Rises After Judge Rejects Forced Sale of 20%-Fee AdX
